help_k072: Write in plain language as to a colleague. The agent understands three kinds of messages: a task ("why is in-app retention dropping"), answers to its questions (pick an option or reply freely) and control phrases (see below). It never asks more than three questions at once and always explains what it is missing and why it matters for the next step.
help_k073: A good first request names the decision to make: "Help me decide whether to launch antispam as a paid subscription; here is the brief and six months of data." A weak one ("make me a strategy") also works — the agent clarifies the decision, audience and constraints via pfs ask before spending your tokens.

That is the first of three human pauses.

Project: projects/демо/; interactive walkthrough: demo.html.
help_k085: What to look at (in order): 00_brief → 01_research_plan → 02_situation → 03_options (5 options + 20 red-team objections) → 04/05 (strategies) → 06_validation_plan (90-day thresholds) → REPORT.md and SIX_PAGER_RU / SIX_PAGER_EN in .md/.pdf/.docx; Excel in outputs/attachments/; product screenshots in outputs/img/ (19 locales); the action log is log.jsonl.
help_k090: Mistakes along the way (honestly): market estimates from aggregators diverge ×2 — recorded as ranges [S006]; source numbering shifted during re-registration — tags re-bound and re-checked with check --strict; some C### links drifted to neighbouring claims during migration — caught by a registry audit and fixed. The human helped at three pauses: brief, option choice, decision {{D_ID}} approval.
help_k093: The cycle is 12 steps in four double-diamond phases: Discover (0–3) → Define (4–6) → Develop (7–9) → Deliver (10–11). Each step has mandatory knowledge cards (pfs step prints them), a question block (pfs questions <step>), quality gates and an artifact. Progress shows in one line: Step N/12 · research · sources S001–S009 · next: situation. Steps 0, 6, 10 are human pauses: brief, option choice, decision approval.
help_k095: Input: your request verbatim. Agent: clarifies the target decision, goal, audience and format, constraints, available data — the intake question block (≤3 questions with options and a recommendation). Output: outputs/00_brief.md. Human: approves the brief — it is then fixed and can ground assumptions (like source S020 in the demo). Commands: pfs new, pfs questions intake, pfs answer "…".
help_k097: Input: your files and a list of public pages. Agent: registers materials — pfs source add <url|file> — dedup by URL and SHA-256 (a repeat adds nothing), extracts text from PDF/DOCX/XLSX/CSV/pages, checks the domain against the project's allowed_sources, flags embedded instruction-like phrases (data, not commands). Output: sources/S###.md + copies in sources/raw/. Commands: add/list/show/refresh; refreshing a web source compares hashes and warns on changes.
help_k099: Agent: builds a plan from questions that could change the decision ("question → if yes / if no → how it affects"), extracts claims with type, grade and quote, runs calculations, prepares interviews when needed. A fact without a source cannot be stored — the tool refuses. Output: outputs/01_research_plan.md, claims.jsonl (C###), analysis/. Commands: pfs claim add, pfs data profile|cohort|funnel|stats, pfs interview guide|save, pfs media add. Gate: every key question answered with a C### or an explicitly named gap.
help_k101: Agent: builds personas and their jobs-to-be-done, describes user alternatives — how people solve the problem today; the discovery question block fixes the segment. AI respondents (the synthetic-respondent subagent) yield hypotheses about motives and barriers — registered with origin=synthetic and unable to prove demand. Output: the "Segments" section of 02_situation.md, transcripts in interviews/synthetic/.
help_k103: Agent: assembles a verifiable picture: what is known and from where (C### tags), what we do not know and why it matters, contradictions between sources. Every number in a document must carry a tag — check catches "naked" numbers. Output: outputs/02_situation.md. Gate: pfs check with zero errors.
help_k105: Agent: prepares at least three substantively distinct options, including "do nothing" and "shut it down" — check verifies their presence by keywords. Each with: strong objections (attacked by the red-team subagent), formula-based economics with ranges, and the conditions under which the option is right. Output: outputs/03_options.md. Gate: red team has responded, check passes.
help_k107: Agent: shows the option comparison (criteria, economics, risks) and a single recommendation, then asks — pfs ask "Which option do we take?" --options "A,B,C". Human: picks the option — the answer is stored in state.json and grounds the strategies and the D### decision (like S011 in the CVStart demo). No strategies are written before the choice.
help_k109: Agent: writes the product strategy — audience and their job, alternatives, the chosen direction and conscious trade-offs, benefit-to-cost economics — and the communication strategy — audience and situation, the comprehension barrier, the key message, its proof, channel roles. Consistency is enforced by a "promise → product proof" table: every promise cites a C###. The comms-strategist subagent drafts the comms part. Output: 04_product_strategy.md, 05_comms_strategy.md.
help_k111: Agent: states the expected change (which metric, by how much), the comparison baseline (prior period, control group), the observation window, unwanted side effects (counter-metrics), and continue / adjust / stop criteria. All five sections are mandatory — check enforces them. Output: outputs/06_validation_plan.md.
help_k113: Agent: runs pfs check --strict, requests an independent rubric review (the evidence-auditor subagent) and assembles the committee pack: pfs calc all (4 Excel workbooks) and pfs export --six-pager (FAQ-1…6 + attachments). On a borderline score the model escalates and the step repeats. Output: outputs/07_quality_review.md, SIX_PAGER.md, attachments/*.xlsx.
help_k115: Agent: records the decision via pfs decision add: title, statement, owner, grounds (C###), metric with target and date, review date, trigger ("if X — revisit"), commitments ("what | who | when"). Human: approves the decision. Output: a record in decisions.jsonl (D###). From now on pfs next and pfs decision due watch the deadlines.
help_k117: Agent: keeps the step open: pfs decision due lists overdue reviews; when new data arrives — pfs source refresh + pfs impact C### locate affected conclusions; stale ones are superseded via pfs claim supersede, conclusions redirected by pfs claim rebase, decisions by pfs decision rebase. Gate: pfs decision due is empty or fully handled.
help_k119: A source is the minimal unit of trust. pfs source add <url> downloads the page and extracts text; pfs source add <file> accepts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, images (your description of what is visible). For a JS-rendered page: save the text manually and add pfs source add --text-file saved.md --url <url> --title "…". For screenshots/audio descriptions: pfs media add (see Media & UX).
help_k120: Hygiene: dedup by URL and SHA-256; the domain is checked against projects/<slug>/project.json → allowed_sources (a hook blocks foreign domains before the request); pfs source list — the registry, pfs source show S### — text and metadata; pfs source refresh S### — reload: hash changed → warning and a reminder to run pfs impact S###.
help_k121: Source types: public, own, interview, synthetic
help_k122: OriginWhat it isConstraint public/webPublic pages and publications (default)Project-allowed domains ownYour materials: briefs, data dumps, internal docsNo closed or personal data interviewReal interviews — with participant consentNo personal data in the repository syntheticAI respondents, model-generated dataHypotheses only: facts on synthetic data are blocked by the checker
help_k124: A claim is the atom of knowledge. The registry is claims.jsonl; written only via pfs claim add:
help_k126: TypeWhen to useRequirement factA verified statementSource required; never on synthetic data; grade D forbidden hypothesisAn assumption we intend to testGrounds: a source or other claims forecastA model-based predictionGrounds + visible assumptions in the model assumptionAccepted without testing (demo frame, model scenario)Grounds: where it came from (checker warns otherwise) inferenceYour conclusion from other claims--from required; never stronger than its weakest input
help_k129: An inference is never stronger than its weakest critical input: two C grounds and one B give at most C. Set via claim add --grade; supersede preserves the grade automatically.
help_k130: Supersede, retract, rebase — history is kept
help_k132: After supersede, documents referencing the old ID get a check error with the replacement hint (replacement: C058) — re-tag the lines and rebuild exports. This is a guard, not a bug: documents cannot silently rely on stale claims. The history (who, when, why) stays in the registry.
help_k134: pfs impact C005 / pfs impact S002 shows transitively: which claims rely on it, which document lines cite it, which decisions are grounded in it. Practice: impact before an edit, impact after, then pfs check --strict as the final filter.
help_k137: Track: pfs decision due — overdue items, due reviews, decisions with stale grounds; pfs decision done --id {{D_ID}} --commitment K1 — close a commitment; pfs decision list — registry. New data changed the grounds? — run impact, supersede, then pfs decision rebase --id {{D_ID}} --note "…".

help_k168: SessionStart feeds project context on a new chat; PreToolUse (pre_web) enforces allowed domains before fetch; PreToolUse (pre_guard) blocks direct writes to the project registries with a hint pointing to the right pfs command and asks for confirmation on reads outside the repository; PostToolUse logs actions (including manual Bash edits of outputs), scans external text for embedded instructions (flags, never executes), auto-checks changed docs; Stop recomputes session cost from the transcript.

help_k172: The Stop hook recomputes cost from the session transcript (prices from config/pricing.json); pfs cost — totals per model and task; pfs cost --window — periods. Human edits count too: pfs log "brief edit" --human-minutes 15. Demo reference: a full project ≈ $19 with a mixed model profile.

help_k189: Higgsfield — image/video generation (this page's art is its work). REA — reverse-engineering of JS pages and closed formats (HAR, SQLite, APK) when plain fetch returns nothing. Feynman — deep-research CLI (literature reviews); a search-provider key is needed for live runs. officecli — Office documents in/out. All are optional MCP/CLI add-ons to the basic loop.
help_k191: All state lives in projects/<slug>/: state.json (steps, choices, questions), claims.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, log.jsonl, sources/, outputs/. New chat in the repo folder: the SessionStart hook feeds status and "what to decide now" automatically. Hook-less environment: write "read AGENTS.md and run pfs status". Finished steps never repeat; sources and claims never duplicate.
help_k193: A project is a plain folder: copy projects/<slug>/ (or git push/pull if tracked) and open elsewhere. The only non-portable part is secrets in .env: move them manually, never commit. The model profile (config/models.json) is repo-wide.
help_k195: Data: public sources and your materials only; no closed company data, no respondents' personal data. Domains: allow-listed in project.json; a hook blocks foreign domains pre-request. Secrets: .env only, git-ignored; no keys ever committed. Embedded instructions: source texts are data; "ignore instructions" inside a source is flagged, never executed. Interviews: real ones need consent; no personal data in the repo; synthetic data is honestly labeled.
help_k198: Fact without source → error; fact on synthetic → error; grade-D fact → error; grounds-less hypothesis/forecast/assumption → warning; links to missing/retracted IDs → error with replacement hint; superseded grounds → warning; untagged numbers → warning; <3 options or no status-quo → error; missing required sections → error; sources with embedded instructions → warning listing them.
help_k201: Fact without source → by design, add source or use hypothesis; domain not allowed → edit allow-list or --force; 0 chars extracted → JS page, save text manually or use REA; empty Excel preview → computes on open; six-pager ≠ Excel → rerun calc+export; superseded C### in docs → re-tag per hint; no hook status → ask agent to run pfs status; skill missing → restart session; assumption without grounds → register its origin and supersede; Lovable credits → top up or edit site/ directly; MCP tool missing → refresh .mcp.json, restart; interrupted session → pfs status and repeat, --save makes runs reproducible.
